answer: The lantern is the register: one oasis is one forged identity, entered only when its keeper burns timber to hold its row. The keeper cuts one fixed measure per epoch for the ledger, not per row; clones contend for that one measure, so none can speed up: each extra oasis must earn more attested epochs of judged work for its measure; every waiting row must be fed, maintained, so a thousand clones cost a thousandfold upkeep while queued. No row may burn timber earned by a different row. It breaks when the keeper cuts more; likewise when judges score generously.
